# Tower Hamlets - council briefing

*Auto-generated from council minutes, 20 May 2026 to 19 August 2026*

## What's dominating the agenda

Housing & Planning leads with 4,837 keyword hits, split between Cabinet's housing strategy and enforcement work and the Strategic Development Committee's planning applications, followed closely by Finance & Budget (4,425, mostly the Extraordinary Overview & Scrutiny Committee's budget scrutiny and Cabinet's outturn reporting) and Licensing & Regulation (4,384, almost entirely premises licence applications through the Licensing Sub-Committee).

## Notable decisions

- Cabinet approved resourcing for the Mayor's Affordable Homes Programme, backing continued delivery of affordable housing across the borough (key decision, approved, 15 Jul).
- Cabinet considered a new supplemental enforcement policy and civil penalties framework under the Renters' Rights Act 2025, giving the council new powers against non-compliant landlords (key decision, 15 Jul).
- Cabinet approved continuing gas and electricity procurement through the Government Commercial Agency framework rather than re-tendering (key decision, approved, 15 Jul).
- Cabinet approved using the extension option on the borough's Waste Reception, Treatment and Recycling Centre Services contract ahead of its 2027 expiry (key decision, approved, 15 Jul).
- Cabinet approved expanding the council's role in the regional fostering recruitment service, taking on the full enquiry-to-approval pathway (key decision, approved, 29 Jul).
- Cabinet approved appointing a main contractor to build the extension to Beatrice Tate Secondary School (key decision, approved, 29 Jul).

## Worth a closer look

- A phased redevelopment at South Quay, Marsh Wall, including demolition of an existing office building, went to the Strategic Development Committee for planning permission (21 Jul). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1538565/file)
- The Grants Determination Sub-Committee signed off the latest Mayor's Community Grants Programme round, funding advice and crisis-support projects tackling the cost of living (1 Jul). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1492234/file)
- External auditors EY presented their provisional audit plan for 2025-26 to the Audit Committee, alongside a progress update on internal-audit standards (23 Jul). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1525365/file)
- The Pension Board reviewed the pension fund's risk register, covering funding and employer-related risks (20 Jul). [source](https://councilgateway.poteris.co.uk/council-api/documents/1538420/file)

## Projects on residents' radar

- **Whitechapel Leisure Centre redevelopment** - Cabinet approved progressing a full rebuild of Whitechapel Leisure Centre, demolishing the current facility and replacing it with a new leisure centre plus new affordable homes on the site (24 Mar). [source](https://democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=7990)
- **Teviot Estate regeneration** - the council approved a Compulsory Purchase Order to acquire land needed for Phase 1 of the Teviot Estate regeneration scheme, working with housing association Poplar HARCA (18 Feb). [source](https://democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=7979)
- **Canary Wharf development with JP Morgan Chase** - Cabinet approved signing a Memorandum of Understanding with JP Morgan Chase covering development plans in Canary Wharf (27 Mar). [source](https://democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=7954)
- **Maltings & Brewster estate safety works** - the council approved an extra £11.3m, taking total costs to £22.8m, to finish removing unsafe external wall insulation and complete structural repairs at the Maltings & Brewster estate, work that has been ongoing since 2017 (27 Mar). [source](https://democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=7957)
- **Tower Hamlets Future Places** - the council published this report setting out its regeneration vision for the borough, intended to attract inward investment and build a pipeline of future development (24 Mar). [source](https://democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk/ieDecisionDetails.aspx?ID=7970)
